comparator.name: Dutch Language and Culture
comparator.academicYear: Coherent prospective 2027–2028 / 2028–2029 / 2029–2030 entry-cohort sequence, checked against adopted 2026–2027 OER
comparator.route: Nederlandse Taal en Cultuur, standard route without study abroad; first-listed literature thesis field
comparator.sourceNotes: A prospective entry-cohort sequence supplies twelve 5-EC compulsory courses in year one, six 5-EC core courses and 30 EC restricted choice of two Faculty of Arts minors in year two, and four 5-EC major courses, a 10-EC thesis and 30 EC open free choice in year three. Total 60+60+60=180. The 2026–27 formally adopted programme-specific OER agrees on the first-year structure and most named second-year courses but lists LET-NTCB221 Psycholinguïstiek in both its concurrent B2 and B3 cohort tables. That single course is counted once in the prospective three-year entry-cohort route, not twice for credit. The later prospective third year contains Verdieping Moderne Nederlandse Letterkunde and Sociolinguïstiek in place of the current-cohort OER third-year list, and is explicitly provisional; it has not been represented as adopted 2026–27 regulation. The thesis is a required 10 EC independent research project; the first-listed Letterkunde thesis is a neutral formal instance among three allowed fields, without changing the programme identity. Zero-credit mentorship and RADAr do not enter the credit total. The optional abroad/educational-minor replacement route is not combined with the standard non-abroad year.
components: Second-year restricted choice of two 15-EC permitted Arts minors; no optional minor content is universally compulsory.

The first-listed formally permitted bachelor thesis field, Dutch literary studies, as one neutral selection among Letterkunde, Taalbeheersing and Taalkunde. The prospective third-year page names Bachelorwerkstuk generically.
Third-year open elective space, which may be used for an internship, a study abroad stay or a permitted educational minor; no optional component is universally required.

routeSelection.route: Nederlandse Taal en Cultuur, standard route without study abroad; first-listed literature thesis field
routeSelection.basis: The target is the generic Dutch Language and Culture bachelor. The ordinary non-abroad route retains a 30-EC minor choice and 30-EC open space, rather than imposing an optional foreign stay, teaching minor or Dutch specialist minor. A literary thesis is the first-listed allowed thesis field, not a claim that all students must choose literature. The prospective coherent cohort sequence avoids counting the same Psycholinguïstiek course twice across OER tables for different concurrent cohorts.

core: Literary analysis, theory, genres and creative expression
Rhetoric, stylistics, persuasion and communication in public and media settings
Historical and cultural context, power, identity, heritage and media
Language acquisition, processing, cognition, variation and human linguistic capacity
Research design, data analysis and evidence synthesis for language, communication and culture
questions: How do literary and media forms represent identity, history and power?
How do people acquire, process and use language?
How do style, rhetoric and media persuade and shape public communication?

candidates.label: Historical Dutch language development
candidates.assessment: UCR offers no historical linguistics, history of Dutch, Dutch phonology or syntax sequence. Introductory Dutch, stylistics and Psycholinguistics do not supply this cumulative Dutch-specific direction.

candidates.label: Dutch-language teaching
candidates.assessment: UCR lacks advanced Dutch-language study, Dutch literature and linguistics preparation, and Dutch subject didactics. The gap is academic content rather than the absence of a teaching qualification alone.

alternatives.label: Literature, rhetoric & cultural interpretation
alternatives.labelReason: Six literature courses, six communication courses including introductory Dutch, four media courses, five history/sociology courses and two cognitive-language courses form the curriculum; the label does not imply advanced Dutch or Dutch literary history.
alternatives.concept: Study literary form, theory and adaptation alongside rhetoric, stylistics, persuasion, media and the historical interpretation of culture, identity and power. Introductory Dutch and Psycholinguistics provide limited language-related study, but the programme does not offer advanced Dutch proficiency, Dutch grammar, historical Dutch linguistics or a Dutch/Flemish literary-history sequence.
progression: Literary, rhetorical, historical, brain-and-behaviour, media and sociological foundations precede advanced literary interpretation, adaptation, persuasive communication, documentary production, historical research and Psycholinguistics. All formal prerequisites and exact planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Language, cognition & public communication
alternatives.labelReason: Six communication courses, eight cognition/psychology courses, three media courses, two sociology courses, two literature courses, philosophy and data analysis make language use, processing and public communication the visible centre.
alternatives.concept: Investigate language as a cognitive, social and persuasive practice through Psycholinguistics, neurobiology, perception, development, stylistics, rhetoric, media, sociology and quantitative research. The curriculum includes only introductory everyday Dutch and therefore addresses language and communication generally rather than reproducing Dutch linguistics, sociolinguistics or advanced Dutch-language study.
progression: Brain-and-behaviour, rhetoric, literary analysis, introductory Dutch, stylistics and neurobiology precede Psycholinguistics, perception, experimental statistics, public rhetoric, advanced cognition, persuasion, development and research synthesis. All formal prerequisites and exact planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: The first programme is organised around literature, cultural interpretation and historical context, with rhetoric and media alongside it. The second makes language processing, cognition and public communication central, replacing eight literature/history/documentary courses with neurobiology, perception, developmental psychology, experimental methods, philosophy of mind and data analysis. Each programme therefore contains 60 EC not found in the other, above the 30-EC floor.

selection.assessment: The literary, rhetorical and cultural programme is the strongest related-fields response to the bachelor’s literature and communication core. The independently evidenced language-and-cognition direction supports a distinct second programme. Creative writing, cultural heritage, arts/politics and power/identity are substantively represented in the closest curriculum rather than relabelled as a third alternative. The next distinct direction, historical Dutch language development, fails because UCR lacks Dutch historical linguistics, phonology and syntax; Dutch-language teaching also lacks the required Dutch academic and didactic preparation. Production stops at two.

blocks: Both directly teach literary analysis; UCR’s introduction is not restricted to Dutch-language literature.
Both examine literature through power and ideology; UCR applies several critical perspectives rather than a Dutch-specific literary corpus.
Both directly address rhetoric and persuasive public communication; UCR does not provide Dutch-specific argumentation training.
Both examine how language choices create meaning across communication and texts; UCR’s stylistics course is not a Dutch-language systems course.
Both directly study persuasive communication; UCR applies the models primarily to climate communication.
Both directly study psycholinguistics and language processing through cognitive and experimental approaches.

notes.text: Radboud Dutch Language and Culture integrates advanced Dutch, Dutch and Flemish literary history, Dutch linguistics, rhetoric and a discipline-specific thesis. UCR can study literature, rhetoric, media, cultural interpretation, Psycholinguistics and basic everyday Dutch, or concentrate on language, cognition and public communication. These are related-fields responses: UCR does not offer advanced academic Dutch, Dutch phonology and syntax, historical Dutch linguistics or a Dutch/Flemish literary-history sequence.
